verifyNotes: Confirm against the official NVIDIA exam page (nvidia.com/en-us/learn/certification/generative-ai-llm-associate/): 1 hour, 50–60 multiple-choice questions, $125, English, online remotely proctored via Certiverse, valid two years (recertify by retaking), pass/fail with no published score. Weights: Core ML and AI Knowledge 30%, Software Development 24%, Experimentation 22%, Data Analysis 14%, Trustworthy AI 10%. Look for an official NCA-GENL study guide PDF linked from the exam page and use its subtopics. Use current NVIDIA product names (NeMo framework and NeMo microservices, NIM, Triton Inference Server / Dynamo-Triton, TensorRT-LLM, RAPIDS cuDF/cuML, NeMo Guardrails, NeMo Curator, NGC); if a product has been renamed, teach the current name and mention the older one. Never copy official sample questions.
name: NVIDIA-Certified Associate: Generative AI LLMs
audience: Developers, data scientists and engineers starting to build generative AI and LLM applications
format: 50–60 multiple-choice questions in 1 hour; online remotely proctored (Certiverse); English. NVIDIA reports pass/fail only and publishes no passing score; this site uses 700 on a 100–1000 scale for its mocks.
scenarios: Customer-support chatbot on an open model
Fine-tuning a small LLM for legal summarisation
GPU-accelerated data prep for a text corpus

domains.name: Core Machine Learning and AI Knowledge
skills: ML and deep learning basics: supervised/unsupervised learning, neural networks, activation and loss functions, gradient descent, overfitting and regularisation
Transformer architecture: tokenisation, embeddings, self-attention, positional encoding, encoder/decoder/decoder-only models, context windows
LLM lifecycle: pre-training, instruction tuning, RLHF/alignment, PEFT (LoRA, p-tuning), prompt engineering (zero/few-shot, chain-of-thought), RAG, decoding (temperature, top-k, top-p)

domains.name: Software Development
skills: Python for ML: NumPy, pandas, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers; building LLM apps with LangChain/LlamaIndex style frameworks
NVIDIA stack: NeMo framework, NIM microservices, Triton Inference Server, TensorRT-LLM, NGC containers; GPU acceleration and CUDA basics; quantisation and inference optimisation
Deploying and serving LLM apps: APIs, containers, batching, latency vs throughput

domains.name: Experimentation
skills: Design experiments: baselines, train/validation/test splits, hyperparameters, tracking runs
Evaluate LLMs: perplexity, BLEU/ROUGE, accuracy/F1, benchmarks, human and LLM-as-judge evaluation; RAG retrieval metrics
Compare fine-tuning vs prompting vs RAG; diagnose failures (hallucination, overfitting, catastrophic forgetting)

domains.name: Data Analysis
skills: Data preparation for LLMs: cleaning, deduplication, filtering, tokenisation, synthetic data (NeMo Curator)
Exploratory analysis and visualisation; GPU-accelerated data science with RAPIDS cuDF/cuML; embeddings and vector databases

domains.name: Trustworthy AI
skills: Bias, fairness, privacy, transparency, model cards, NVIDIA Trustworthy AI principles
Guardrails and safety: NeMo Guardrails, content moderation, prompt injection, jailbreaks, hallucination mitigation
